reward_vs_leaving_analysis.status: done (2026-09-16), timing bug fixed same day (user-caught), NULL RESULT after FDR correction (unchanged by the fix)
reward_vs_leaving_analysis.script: scripts/reward_vs_leaving_responsiveness_session.py (fresh reconstruction of the 20260901_085606 methodology -- see its docstring and WORKFLOW.md 2026-09-16 entries; original script was never saved)
reward_vs_leaving_analysis.method: per-GOOD-unit Mann-Whitney U test, spike count in a 0.5s window after event, rewarded trials (aligned to water_L/water_R delivery) vs non-rewarded completed trials (aligned to the LAST poke-Out event on the chosen side port, bounded to before that trial's own ITI state = physical port-leaving). Trial-consistency filters per condition: >=20 total spikes, >=15 responsive trials, top-2-trials spike share <=40%. Benjamini-Hochberg FDR across all tested units.
reward_vs_leaving_analysis.bug_found_and_fixed: User asked 'are you sure you have the correct time point from bpod?' -- investigation found the original 'port-leaving' time (unbounded max() over ALL poke-Out events in the trial) could pick up a spurious later poke during the ITI or even the next trial, since a trial's event window runs a fixed 10s past its last state and commonly overlaps the next trial (confirmed for real trials, e.g. trial 18: true departure at t=4.2522s just before skipped_feedback at t=4.3341s, but the unbounded search picked t=5.093s instead, well into the next trial). Also discovered along the way: 'non-rewarded completed' trials are NOT all wrong-side choices (unrewarded_Lin/Rin state) -- some are CORRECT-side choices (rewarded_Lin/Rin state) where the rat left too early and forfeited the reward before delivery; both converge on the same ITI state afterward. Fixed by bounding the Out-event search to before that trial's own ITI state start (general fix, not hardcoded to 'skipped_feedback', so it stays correct even for a session where timeOut_IncorrectChoice actually fires). Verified the water_L/water_R reward-time point separately against TASK_TIMELINE.md's documented state sequence -- that one was already correct (valve opens exactly at that state's start).
reward_vs_leaving_analysis.result: AFTER THE FIX: 166/183 good units tested, 0 FDR-significant (alpha=0.05) -- same null conclusion as before the fix, but individual unit rankings/values shifted (e.g. new top candidates unit 37/48 appeared; unit 229 stayed top, min p_fdr=0.340 vs the pre-fix 0.394). 12/166 nominal uncorrected p<0.05. This confirms the null result is real and not an artifact of the timing bug.
reward_vs_leaving_analysis.caveat: This null result should NOT be directly compared to 20260901_085606's 6-leading-units finding as if they're the same kind of measurement -- that session's result came from Phy-curated, manually-verified 'good' units on authoritative synced data; this session's 'good' units are automatic-classifier-only (no human/Phy check yet). A different, weaker, or absent result here could reflect real session-to-session variability, or could partly reflect noisier/less-precise unit curation -- can't disambiguate those two until this session also goes through Phy. NOTE: if 20260901_085606's original reward-vs-leaving script similarly used an unbounded last-Out-event search, it may have the SAME bug -- not yet checked, since that original script was never found/saved (see WORKFLOW.md 1f-pre).

reward_pre_post_responsiveness_analysis.status: done (2026-09-16), NULL RESULT after FDR correction
reward_pre_post_responsiveness_analysis.method: per-unit paired Wilcoxon signed-rank test (rewarded trials only), spike count in [-600,-100)ms before reward delivery vs [+100,+600)ms after, same trial paired. Ran over ALL 461 non-noise units (183 good + 278 mua, quality_label kept in output), not just good units, per explicit user request ('for all neurons'). Trial-consistency filters: >=10 total spikes (pre+post combined), >=15 trials with a nonzero pre/post difference, top-2-trials' |diff| share <=40% of total |diff|. BH-FDR across all tested units.
reward_pre_post_responsiveness_analysis.result: 426/461 units passed the trial-consistency filters and were tested. 0 FDR-significant (alpha=0.05) -- 0 increase, 0 decrease. 21/426 units had nominal uncorrected p<0.05 (essentially exactly the 5% chance-level rate for 426 tests -- min p=0.0030, unit 33) and 4/426 had p<0.01. PSTHs of the top 6 nominal candidates (outputs/reward_pre_post_top6_20260911_100049.png) show wide, overlapping SEM bands around the small pre/post differences -- consistent with a genuine flat null, not a methodology bug.
reward_pre_post_responsiveness_analysis.caveat: Same pre-Phy-curation caveat as reward_vs_leaving_analysis above applies here too.

left_right_cue_response_analysis.status: done (2026-09-16), NULL RESULT after FDR correction (closest call of the 4 analyses so far)
left_right_cue_response_analysis.script: scripts/left_right_cue_response_session.py -- SUPERSEDES scripts/left_right_choice_period_responsiveness_session.py (kept for reference but its left-vs-right-difference approach was wrong for the actual question asked, see WORKFLOW.md 2026-09-16 entry)
left_right_cue_response_analysis.method: Per-unit paired Wilcoxon signed-rank test, baseline (stay_Cin state, pre-cue fixation, median 0.296s) vs response (wait_Sin state, cue-end to choice-poke+0.2s, median 0.466s), run SEPARATELY for left-choice and right-choice completed trials (independent FDR per side) over all 461 non-noise units. Only TrialCompleted==1 trials with decision time (cue-end to poke) <3.0s (explicit user-specified cutoff; no-op this session, max observed 1.11s). Both windows compared as per-trial firing RATE (duration varies per trial). Trial-consistency filters per side: >=10 total spikes, >=8 nonzero-diff trials, top-2 |diff| share <=40%.
left_right_cue_response_analysis.result: 565 valid trials (239 left, 326 right). Left family: 430/461 tested, 0 FDR-significant (30/430 nominal p<0.05, min p_fdr=0.354). Right family: 433/461 tested, 0 FDR-significant (22/433 nominal p<0.05, min p_fdr=0.116). Closest calls: units 135 (good) and 118 (mua), both RIGHT family, tied at p_fdr=0.116 -- their PSTHs show a visible post-cue ramp not seen as clearly in the other 3 analyses' top candidates. Still not significant.

superseded_first_pass.why_wrong: Only tested whether firing during the decision window DIFFERED between left- and right-choice trials (Mann-Whitney, left rate vs right rate) -- this misses a neuron that responds equally strongly to BOTH sides (no left-vs-right difference at all, but still a real choice-locked response). User caught this and clarified the actual ask needs a baseline comparison per side, not a left-vs-right difference test.

left_right_cue_response_analysis.caveat: Same pre-Phy-curation caveat as the other analyses on this page applies here too.
